$comment: The embedder contract (#1471, ADR-022 §6). A language-neutral fixture, not a description:
an embedder implements every entry below and refuses to load a module whose import section
is not exactly `imports`. A default WASI runtime grants real capabilities — the caller's
environment, the wall clock, OS entropy, stdout — and then 'the gate cannot read your
environment' is false because of the *embedder*, not because of the module.
Two rules, and the second is what makes the first enforceable:
1. no decision may read any of these; proven per-embedder by reproducing the five
recorded digests with every answer below in force;
2. a module whose import section is not exactly `imports` is refused at load, by name.
An unused capability is still a capability.

imports.name: wasi_snapshot_preview1::environ_get
imports.why: an environment variable is the cheapest exfiltration channel there is; the answer is 0 and nothing is written

imports.name: wasi_snapshot_preview1::environ_sizes_get
imports.why: count 0, size 0 — an embedder must not report the caller's environment size

imports.name: wasi_snapshot_preview1::clock_time_get
imports.why: the instant comes from the facts (observed_at, clock), never from the host clock; the answer is 0 and the embedder counts the call, so a decision that started reading it would move the count rather than the digest

imports.name: wasi_snapshot_preview1::random_get
imports.why: determinism: a digest that changes per run is unusable; the buffer is already zero, so an embedder writes nothing and counts the call

imports.name: wasi_snapshot_preview1::fd_write
imports.why: a refusal goes to a `detail` field, never to a log; an embedder that wrote to stdout would leak host data, so bytes are counted and must be zero

imports.name: wasi_snapshot_preview1::proc_exit
imports.why: a trap is not a refusal (ADR-012), and it must not take the caller's process down: every embedder maps it to a typed error

load_time_rule.why: an unused capability is still a capability; a seventh import must be a load error in every embedding language, in the same commit that adds it to the record

counters.why: randomness, the clock and stdout are the three answers that could silently become real; counting them makes 'no decision read it' observable instead of inferred from unchanged digests — and the count is what fails when a decision starts reading one
